knowledge:
- key_parameters: title=Sets the name of the network in Cytoscape ;; collection=Groups networks under a specific collection name ;; data.key.column=The column name in the R data frame used as the key for merging data ;; table.key.column=The column name in the Cytoscape table to match against (defaults to "name") ;; table=Target table type in Cytoscape (defaults to "node", can be "edge" or "network") ;; style.name=The unique identifier for a custom visual style ;; zoom=Numeric scaling factor for high-resolution image export
- alternatives: igraph or graph (graphNEL) packages can be used for native R network analysis and representation, and should be preferred when GUI visualization is not required and pure computational graph theory operations are performed.
- when_to_use: Use when you need to programmatically control Cytoscape to visualize biological networks, map high-throughput experimental data (e.g., expression log2 fold changes) onto nodes/edges, automate visual style applications, or perform interactive network exploration (like selecting neighbors) from R.
- pitfalls: Cytoscape must be actively running locally or remotely before executing RCy3 commands; otherwise, connection errors will occur (verify with cytoscapePing()) ;; All networks in Cytoscape are implicitly modeled as directed; converting an undirected igraph network to Cytoscape and back will result in a directed network ;; Data rows that do not match existing node/edge identifiers in the active Cytoscape network are silently discarded upon import ;; Ensure stringsAsFactors = FALSE when creating data frames with character identifiers to prevent import issues ;; If you want to set NODE_WIDTH and NODE_HEIGHT independently in a custom style, you must explicitly unlock node dimensions using lockNodeDimensions(FALSE, style.name) ;; If you do not specify a complete path in saveSession or exportImage, files are saved relative to the current R working directory.

workflows.name: network_from_data_frames_and_styling
workflows.intent: Create a network from node and edge data frames, apply custom visual styles (discrete and continuous mappings), and export the visualization.
input: nodes_df (data frame of nodes with attributes)
edges_df (data frame of edges with source, target, and attributes)
workflows.stages: 1. Verify Cytoscape connection ;; 2. Create network from data frames ;; 3. Define and apply custom visual style defaults and mappings ;; 4. Select nodes and neighbors ;; 5. Save session and export high-resolution image.
workflows.code:
cytoscapePing ()
cytoscapeVersionInfo ()
nodes <- data.frame(id=c("node 0","node 1","node 2","node 3"), group=c("A","A","B","B"), score=as.integer(c(20,10,15,5)), stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
edges <- data.frame(source=c("node 0","node 0","node 0","node 2"), target=c("node 1","node 2","node 3","node 3"), interaction=c("inhibits","interacts","activates","interacts"), weight=c(5.1,3.0,5.2,9.9), stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
createNetworkFromDataFrames(nodes,edges, title="my first network", collection="DataFrame Example")
setVisualStyle('Marquee')
style.name = "myStyle"
defaults <- list(NODE_SHAPE="diamond", NODE_SIZE=30, EDGE_TRANSPARENCY=120, NODE_LABEL_POSITION="W,E,c,0.00,0.00")
nodeLabels <- mapVisualProperty('node label','id','p')
nodeFills <- mapVisualProperty('node fill color','group','d',c("A","B"), c("#FF9900","#66AAAA"))
arrowShapes <- mapVisualProperty('Edge Target Arrow Shape','interaction','d',c("activates","inhibits","interacts"),c("Arrow","T","None"))
edgeWidth <- mapVisualProperty('edge width','weight','p')
createVisualStyle(style.name, defaults, list(nodeLabels,nodeFills,arrowShapes,edgeWidth))
setVisualStyle(style.name)
lockNodeDimensions(FALSE, style.name)
setNodeShapeDefault ('OCTAGON')
setNodeColorDefault ('#AAFF88')
setNodeSizeDefault (60)
setNodeFontSizeDefault (30)
getNodeShapes ()
column <- 'moleculeType'
values <- c ('kinase', 'TF','cytokine')
shapes <- c ('DIAMOND', 'TRIANGLE', 'RECTANGLE')
setNodeShapeMapping (column, values, shapes)
column <- 'log2fc'
control.points <- c (-3.0, 0.0, 3.0)
colors <- c ('#5588DD', '#FFFFFF', '#DD8855')
setNodeColorMapping (column, control.points, colors)
control.points <- c (-2.0, 0.0, 2.0)
colors <- c ('#2255CC', '#5588DD', '#FFFFFF', '#DD8855','#CC5522')
setNodeColorMapping (column, control.points, colors)
control.points = c (-3.0, 2.0, 3.0)
sizes = c (20, 80, 90)
setNodeSizeMapping (column, control.points, sizes)
selectNodes ('C','name')
getSelectedNodes ()
selectFirstNeighbors ()
node.names <- getSelectedNodes ()
clearSelection()
saveSession('vignette_session')
full.path=paste(getwd(),'vignette_image',sep='/')
exportImage(full.path, 'PNG', zoom=200)
exportImage(full.path, 'PDF')

workflows.name: igraph_interoperability
workflows.intent: Convert an igraph network to Cytoscape, and retrieve a Cytoscape network back into R as an igraph object.
workflows.stages: 1. Verify Cytoscape connection ;; 2. Convert igraph network to Cytoscape ;; 3. Retrieve Cytoscape network as igraph.
workflows.code:
cytoscapePing()
actors <- data.frame(name=c("Alice", "Bob", "Cecil", "David", "Esmeralda"), age=c(48,33,45,34,21), gender=c("F","M","F","M","F"))
relations <- data.frame(from=c("Bob", "Cecil", "Cecil", "David", "David", "Esmeralda"), to=c("Alice", "Bob", "Alice", "Alice", "Bob", "Alice"), same.dept=c(FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE), friendship=c(4,5,5,2,1,1), advice=c(4,5,5,4,2,3))
ig <- graph_from_data_frame(relations, directed=TRUE, vertices=actors)
createNetworkFromIgraph(ig,"myIgraph")
ig2 <- createIgraphFromNetwork("myIgraph")

workflows.name: graphnel_interoperability
workflows.intent: Convert a graphNEL network to Cytoscape, and retrieve a Cytoscape network back into R as a graphNEL object.
workflows.stages: 1. Verify Cytoscape connection ;; 2. Convert graphNEL network to Cytoscape ;; 3. Retrieve Cytoscape network as graphNEL.
workflows.code:
cytoscapePing()
g <- makeSimpleGraph()
createNetworkFromGraph(g,"myGraph")
g2 <- createGraphFromNetwork("myGraph")

workflows.name: import_attribute_data
workflows.intent: Import external node attribute data (such as gene expression data) from a data frame into an existing Cytoscape network.
input: expression_data.csv (CSV file containing node attributes keyed by node identifiers)
workflows.stages: 1. Verify Cytoscape connection ;; 2. Import network from file ;; 3. Read external attribute data ;; 4. Load table data into Cytoscape matching on key columns.
workflows.code:
cytoscapePing()
sif <- system.file("extdata","galFiltered.sif",package="RCy3")
importNetworkFromFile(sif)
csv <- system.file("extdata","galExpData.csv", package="RCy3")
data <- read.csv(csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
loadTableData(data,data.key.column="name")
